drafted_from: tool:github:ffmpeg-ffmpeg's row in tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json (job, run, get_it, needs) and its sources row in sources.json; the command is the row's own run line with synthetic names filled in. What it prints or writes is read from the tool's documented behavior; the folder test test/index-github-tools.test.mjs only checks the row, never runs FFmpeg.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Use FFmpeg on my computer to convert: the file is interview.mp4." It reads the row, installs FFmpeg if it is missing, runs it on that one file and shows you what it made.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: FFmpeg is a program that runs on the person's own computer and works on the one file or address it is handed.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Use FFmpeg on interview.mp4". It reads the row with run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:ffmpeg-ffmpeg"}.

2. It checks that nothing else is on your computer, and if FFmpeg is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg.git ; brew install ffmpeg (macOS), or apt install ffmpeg (Linux), or the builds linked from ffmpeg.org.
3. It runs the row's command with your file in place of {input} and where the result goes in place of {output}: ffmpeg -i interview.mp4 interview.mp3
4. Read what it shows you and open the result. Trillion runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: FFmpeg on a 5 minute video file
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json: tool:github:ffmpeg-ffmpeg runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got FFmpeg in, the command line: ffmpeg -i interview.mp4 interview.mp3  (synthetic input: a 5 minute video file).
worked_examples.hands_back: ffmpeg prints its build banner and the stream details, then ends with a progress line such as "size=4608KiB time=00:05:00.00 bitrate= 128.0kbits/s" and leaves interview.mp3 (the sound only) beside the video.
